predecessors.name: Principality of Achaea
predecessors.text: Corinth, mortgaged to Nerio Acciaioli after 1365 by Angelo Acciaioli and confirmed hereditary in 1371; Nerio 'lord of the town of Corinth' in November 1372

predecessors.name: Catalan Company
predecessors.text: Megara (1375), the lower town of Athens (1385), Thebes (1385, disputed), the Acropolis (2 May 1388) and Neopatras (1390), taken from the Catalan Company and the Navarrese Company

successors.name: Ottoman Empire
successors.text: Athens (the Acropolis surrendered in June 1458; Mehmed II entered in August 1458) and Thebes (Franco died in 1460); the page's succession table: 'Annexed by Ottoman Empire'

rulers.name: Nerio I Acciaioli
rulers.title: lord of Corinth, duke of Athens

ledger.x: November 1372: Nerio Acciaioli, lord of Corinth.
Late 1374 or early 1375: Nerio takes Megara.
1385: Nerio takes the lower town of Athens.
1385: Thebes (disputed).
1388: the seat moves from Corinth to Athens, the infobox capital.
2 May 1388: Nerio's troops take the Acropolis.
1390: Nerio takes Neopatras.
22 May 1390: Nerio cedes Megara to Venice.
Late 1393: Bayezid I takes Neopatras.
11 January 1394: Ladislaus of Naples invests Nerio I with the Duchy of Athens.
September 1394: Corinth leaves the Acciaioli.
ledger.cpn: County Palatine of Cephalonia and Zakynthos (Tocco)

ledger.x: 18 March 1395: Venice annexes Athens.
First half of 1402: Antonio takes the lower town of Athens in a surprise attack.
January or February 1403: the Acropolis surrenders.
1403: Antonio I restores the Acciaioli in Athens ('Antonio I (1402-1435), restored', Duchy page).
1456: the Ottomans take Athens but not the Acropolis.
June 1458: the Acropolis surrenders.
June 1458: Athens passes to the Ottomans; Mehmed II entered the city in August 1458 and let Franco keep Thebes 'as his vassal'.
August 1458: the dukes' seat moves from Athens to Thebes, where Mehmed II let Franco remain as his vassal.
1460: Franco dies and Thebes is annexed.
1460: the last Acciaioli duke is dead and the duchy is gone.

wars.name: Acciaioli conquest of Athens
wars.outcome: Nerio took the lower town of Athens in 1385 and the Acropolis on 2 May 1388, ending Catalan rule in Athens; plague forced him to withdraw to Thebes in 1386-87.

wars.name: Bayezid I's invasion of Thessaly
wars.outcome: Bayezid captured Neopatras and Livadeia in late 1393; Nerio agreed in early 1394 to pay an annual tribute.

wars.name: Venetian-Acciaioli struggle for Athens
wars.outcome: Venice annexed Athens in 1395 and held it to 1402; Antonio I took the lower town in 1402 and the Acropolis in early 1403; a compromise of 31 March 1405 recognised his rule.

wars.name: Ottoman conquest of the Duchy of Athens
wars.outcome: Turahanoglu Omer Bey conquered the remnants of the duchy in 1456; Franco held the Acropolis until June 1458; Mehmed II entered Athens in August 1458 and let Franco keep Thebes as a vassal until 1460.

certainty.note: No treaty line is on any page opened.
